newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese TMA resumes flights after 3-month halt.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese TMA resumes flights after 3-month halt.

text.p: Lebanon's troubled cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines (TMA) said on Wednesday it will resume its flights after a three-month stoppage for administrative re-structuring.
TMA's 86 pilots returned to work on Wednesday and the first flight will be to London tomorrow, TMA official said

The company invited shareholders on November 10 to subscribe to a new share issue to increase its capital to 60 billion Lebanese pounds from six million. It said subscriptions would be open from November 14 to December 14.
TMA suspended activities on August 5 and two of its six aircraft are on lease to Kuwait Airlines. Its 240 ground workers resumed work on November 12.

TMA is owned by the Lebanese company Air Investment, which is 73 percent owned by prominent banker Farid Raphael. Former education minister Najib Abu Haidar holds 10 percent, Druze leader Walid Jumblatt six percent and financier George Yaacoub five percent. The rest is owned by small investors.
